question: Should the scoped SQLite and cache implementation land once the branch is refreshed and the exact head passes required checks, accepting its bounded session-state visibility risk?
rationale: Tests and live proof support the implementation, but choosing to change the canonical persisted-read path for controller and child session state requires an owner to accept the remaining cross-process and cache-coherence risk.

options.title: Refresh, verify, and land
options.body: Rebase or refresh onto current main, rerun the focused registry proof and required checks, then merge after an Agents owner confirms the state invariants.

options.title: Pause for broader runtime proof
options.body: Hold the PR until a multi-process Gateway scenario demonstrates controller and child reads across concurrent writer and reader processes.

recommendation.title: Refresh, verify, and land
recommendation.body: Rebase or refresh onto current main, rerun the focused registry proof and required checks, then merge after an Agents owner confirms the state invariants.

likelyOwner.reason: Their recent agents/subagent runtime work makes them the strongest available owner for the session-state merge-risk decision.
